title: Design System: Warp Overwatch: Lane Vanguards

signal-blue.note: Load-bearing: must match the blue color-locked tap. Not available for aesthetic tuning.

arc-white.note: Player node 02. A hue and an absence of hue, so the two nodes stay separable peripherally.

chrome-cyan.note: The console's own light. Never on anything the player controls or must match.

breach-red.note: The threat baseline every other hazard color is read against.

armor-violet.note: Appears only where the answer is dual-node coordination.

payload-gold.note: The Gold Rule — gains only. Never a hazard, never decoration.

secure-green.note: Never appears on a live threat.

ember-amber.note: The fry/reboot language. Means 'broken and coming back'.

null-graphite.note: The calmest body in the game and the most dangerous. Never brighten it.

bore-void.note: The true base of the world — deep navy-black behind the tunnel circuitry.

hull-black.note: Shell and native theme color. A half-step lighter than Bore Void so the canvas reads as a lit object.

panel-glass.note: Always translucent (92%) — the tunnel must stay faintly visible through chrome.

body-ice.note: Reading copy on discs and cards, set at 88% opacity.

display.purpose: Brand wordmark, level titles, boss title stamps. Shrink-to-fit, never wrap.

headline.purpose: Briefing disc titles and victory report headings.

title.purpose: Console header bands. Widest tracking in the system — reads as an engraved label.

body.purpose: Case-file logs and card copy. Tight 3px extra leading because copy sits inside a circle.

label.purpose: Actions, mode names, TAP TO CONTINUE, stamped callouts.

caption.purpose: Sub-captions under mode keys and pad states.

readout.purpose: Machine telemetry only — range, boot status, hex garnish. Never language the player must comprehend.

shadows.name: panel-bloom
shadows.purpose: Console panels only. Disabled under the lowFX watchdog. This system's only 'shadow' is additive light.

shadows.name: signal-halo
shadows.purpose: Nodes, pickups, pulse waves. Radial falloff from the source color to fully transparent.

shadows.name: halation
shadows.purpose: Highest-energy moments only — arc discharge, pulse fire. Pairs with a long specular streak across the body.

shadows.name: contact-line
shadows.purpose: Seating and levitation read as a tight dark line, never as a glow gap.

shadows.name: vignette
shadows.purpose: Cached finishing pass, applied before film grain. lowFX-gated.

motion.name: ease-out-back
motion.purpose: Briefing disc zoom-in (0.28s). Lands with a breath of overshoot (1.70158).

motion.name: disc-out
motion.purpose: Briefing disc retreat — faster than entry so dismissal feels responsive.

motion.name: smoothstep
motion.purpose: The world's default easing, used for the boot ring fly-in and every depth transition.

motion.name: wheel-spin
motion.purpose: Mode wheel spins out clockwise and crossfades on screen change; back reverses.

motion.name: panels-in
motion.purpose: Route map: relay list flies in from the left staggered, dossier from the right.

motion.name: teletype
motion.purpose: Case-file log typing, with a tick tone every other character.

motion.name: prompt-pulse
motion.purpose: TAP TO CONTINUE and other waiting prompts.

breakpoints.name: none
breakpoints.purpose: Radial composition scales continuously from min(W,H). The far ring is pinned at 2.5x the node ring so the reaction window is identical on every aspect ratio — a fairness constraint, not a layout preference.

components.name: Console Panel
components.description: The base container: glass over dark metal with a luminous header band and floating target-lock brackets.
components.html:
SYSTEM STATUS
NODE 01 — ONLINE
NODE 02 — ONLINE
DOCK CONFIRMED
components.css: .ds-panel { --cut: 16px; position: relative; width: 280px; padding: 7px; font-family: Audiowide, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-panel-body { position: relative; background: rgba(110,210,255,0.65); clip-path: polygon(var(--cut) 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - var(--cut)), calc(100% - var(--cut)) 100%, 0 100%, 0 var(--cut)); filter: drop-shadow(0 0 16px rgba(95,215,255,0.55)); } .ds-panel-body::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 1.5px; background: rgba(4,14,30,0.92); clip-path: polygon(calc(var(--cut) - 1px) 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - var(--cut) + 1px), calc(100% - var(--cut) + 1px) 100%, 0 100%, 0 calc(var(--cut) - 1px)); } .ds-panel-head { position: relative; height: 32px; line-height: 32px; padding: 0 20px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 3px; color: #cfeeff; background: linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(80,190,255,0.35) 0%, rgba(80,190,255,0.02) 85%); border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(120,220,255,0.5); } .ds-panel-content { position: relative; padding: 16px 20px 20px; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 10px; line-height: 1.6; letter-spacing: 0.5px; color: rgba(190,225,255,0.88); } .ds-panel-bracket { position: absolute; width: 14px; height: 14px; border: 1.5px solid rgba(120,220,255,0.55); } .ds-bk-tl { top: 0; left: 0; border-right: 0; border-bottom: 0; } .ds-bk-tr { top: 0; right: 0; border-left: 0; border-bottom: 0; } .ds-bk-br { bottom: 0; right: 0; border-left: 0; border-top: 0; } .ds-bk-bl { bottom: 0; left: 0; border-right: 0; border-top: 0; }

components.name: Key
components.description: The standard action key. Cut-corner plate, 38px tall, press micro-feedback. No hover state — this is a touch product.
components.css: .ds-key { --cut: 8px; position: relative; height: 38px; padding: 0 28px; border: 0; background: rgba(120,200,255,0.55); color: #dff2ff; font-family: Audiowide, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 3px; cursor: pointer; clip-path: polygon(var(--cut) 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - var(--cut)), calc(100% - var(--cut)) 100%, 0 100%, 0 var(--cut)); transition: color 120ms linear, transform 90ms ease-out; } .ds-key::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 1.2px; z-index: -1; background: rgba(20,44,72,0.9); clip-path: polygon(calc(var(--cut) - 1px) 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - var(--cut) + 1px), calc(100% - var(--cut) + 1px) 100%, 0 100%, 0 calc(var(--cut) - 1px)); transition: background 120ms linear; } .ds-key:focus-visible { outline: 0; background: rgba(140,230,255,0.9); color: #eafaff; } .ds-key:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(0.985); color: #eafaff; } .ds-key:active::before { background: rgba(29,61,97,0.95); }

components.name: Destructive Key
components.description: Oxide-red variant for irreversible actions (campaign reset). Same silhouette, different livery — the shape never signals danger, the color does.
components.css: .ds-key-danger { --cut: 8px; position: relative; height: 38px; padding: 0 28px; border: 0; background: rgba(255,120,120,0.85); color: #ffd9d9; font-family: Audiowide, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 3px; cursor: pointer; clip-path: polygon(var(--cut) 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - var(--cut)), calc(100% - var(--cut)) 100%, 0 100%, 0 var(--cut)); transition: color 120ms linear, transform 90ms ease-out; } .ds-key-danger::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 1.2px; z-index: -1; background: rgba(120,26,26,0.92); clip-path: polygon(calc(var(--cut) - 1px) 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - var(--cut) + 1px), calc(100% - var(--cut) + 1px) 100%, 0 100%, 0 calc(var(--cut) - 1px)); transition: background 120ms linear; } .ds-key-danger:focus-visible { outline: 0; background: #ff9a9a; color: #fff; } .ds-key-danger:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(0.985); } .ds-key-danger:active::before { background: rgba(150,34,34,0.96); }

components.name: Briefing Disc
components.description: The signature component. Story and instruction arrive as a disc that flies up to the operator, dissolving into the bore at its rim rather than ending on an edge.
components.html:
CASE FILE // LC-2209
THE CONTRACT

Meridian Haulage must deliver evidence
to Lane Command across one warp lane.
You were hired to keep it clean.
Interdictors are already in the lane.

components.css: @keyframes ds-disc-in { from { transform: scale(0.3); opacity: 0; } to { transform: scale(1); opacity: 1; } } @keyframes ds-disc-drift { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } } @keyframes ds-prompt-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 0.2; } 50% { opacity: 0.8; } } .ds-disc { position: relative; width: 320px; height: 320px; display: grid; place-items: center; text-align: center; font-family: Audiowide, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 50%, rgba(6,11,24,0.93) 25%, rgba(5,9,20,0.88) 82%, rgba(5,9,20,0) 100%); border-radius: 50%; animation: ds-disc-in 280ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) both; } .ds-disc-rim { position: absolute; inset: 3%; border-radius: 50%; border: 1.5px solid rgba(120,200,255,0.3); } .ds-disc-rim::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -1.5px; border-radius: 50%; border: 2.5px solid transparent; background: conic-gradient(rgba(140,230,255,0.75) 0 7%, transparent 0 25%, rgba(140,230,255,0.75) 0 32%, transparent 0 50%, rgba(140,230,255,0.75) 0 57%, transparent 0 75%, rgba(140,230,255,0.75) 0 82%, transparent 0) border-box; mask: linear-gradient(#000 0 0) padding-box exclude, linear-gradient(#000 0 0); animation: ds-disc-drift 42s linear infinite; } .ds-disc-inner { position: relative; width: 60%; } .ds-disc-kicker { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 3px; color: rgba(255,210,74,0.8); margin-bottom: 26px; } .ds-disc-title { font-size: 22px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #eafaff; margin-bottom: 20px; } .ds-disc-body { font-size: 15px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.2; color: rgba(190,225,255,0.88); margin-bottom: 30px; } .ds-disc-prompt { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 3px; color: rgba(140,230,255,1); animation: ds-prompt-pulse 1.6s ease-in-out infinite; }

components.name: Dial Gauge
components.description: The player's only control and the clearest expression of the gauge grammar: a wide translucent track between two thin rails, with eight compass ticks.
components.css: .ds-dial { --node: 80,170,255; position: relative; width: 132px; height: 132px; border-radius: 50%; background: rgba(10,20,45,0.35); } .ds-dial-track { position: absolute; inset: 12px; border-radius: 50%; border: 15px solid rgba(var(--node),0.16); transition: border-color 140ms linear; } .ds-dial:hover .ds-dial-track { border-color: rgba(var(--node),0.3); } .ds-dial-rail { position: absolute; border-radius: 50%; border: 1.5px solid rgba(var(--node),0.4); } .ds-rail-in { inset: 25px; } .ds-rail-out { inset: 5px; } .ds-dial-ticks { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: repeating-conic-gradient(from 0deg, rgba(var(--node),0.5) 0deg 1.2deg, transparent 1.2deg 45deg), repeating-conic-gradient(from 22.5deg, rgba(var(--node),0.28) 0deg 1deg, transparent 1deg 45deg); mask: radial-gradient(circle, transparent 0 42%, #000 42% 54%, transparent 54%); } .ds-dial-thumb { position: absolute; top: 4px; left: 50%; width: 13px; height: 13px; margin-left: -6.5px; border-radius: 50%; background: #50aaff; box-shadow: 0 0 14px rgba(80,170,255,0.9); }

components.name: Mode Sector
components.description: The home screen's navigation: the ring's interior cut into color-coded sectors. Flattened here to a key; in-game the label curves along its own slice.
components.css: @keyframes ds-mode-breathe { 0%, 100% { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgba(126,226,98,0.55); } 50% { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgba(126,226,98,0.95), 0 0 22px rgba(126,226,98,0.28); } } .ds-modes { display: flex; gap: 12px; font-family: Audiowide, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-mode { --cut: 12px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; align-items: flex-start; padding: 16px 20px; border: 0; background: rgba(8,18,34,0.9); cursor: pointer; text-align: left; clip-path: polygon(var(--cut) 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - var(--cut)), calc(100% - var(--cut)) 100%, 0 100%, 0 var(--cut)); } .ds-mode-name { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 3px; } .ds-mode-cap { font-size: 9px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.5px; } .ds-mode-primary { color: #7ee262; animation: ds-mode-breathe 2.4s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-mode-primary .ds-mode-cap { color: rgba(126,226,98,0.65); } .ds-mode-primary:focus-visible { outline: 0; color: #a5f08c; } .ds-mode-locked { color: rgba(160,200,240,0.35); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgba(160,200,240,0.18); cursor: default; } .ds-mode-locked .ds-mode-cap { color: rgba(160,200,240,0.28); }

components.name: Arc Node Band
components.description: The system's biggest unification: the player's node is a lit sector of the ring bounded by two machined bus-bars, and its angular span IS the zap tolerance. Visual equals mechanic.
components.css: @keyframes ds-arc-breathe { 0%, 100% { opacity: 0.72; } 50% { opacity: 1; } } .ds-ring { position: relative; width: 240px; height: 240px; } .ds-ring-band { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: conic-gradient(from -110deg, #2c3340, #444d5c 18%, #1a1f28 38%, #383f4d 62%, #12161d 82%, #2c3340); mask: radial-gradient(circle, transparent 0 40%, #000 40% 50%, transparent 50%); } .ds-ring-band::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: linear-gradient(200deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.16) 0%, transparent 42%); mask: radial-gradient(circle, transparent 0 40%, #000 40% 50%, transparent 50%); } .ds-arc { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 50%; mask: radial-gradient(circle, transparent 0 40%, #000 40% 50%, transparent 50%); animation: ds-arc-breathe 3.1s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-arc-blue { background: conic-gradient(from 162deg, transparent 0 0%, rgba(80,170,255,0.25) 0 3%, rgba(140,205,255,0.95) 0 7%, rgba(80,170,255,0.25) 0 10%, transparent 0); filter: drop-shadow(0 0 12px rgba(80,170,255,0.8)); } .ds-arc-white { background: conic-gradient(from -18deg, transparent 0 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0.25) 0 3%, rgba(255,255,255,0.95) 0 7%, rgba(255,255,255,0.25) 0 10%, transparent 0); filter: drop-shadow(0 0 12px rgba(220,240,255,0.75)); animation-delay: -1.4s; } .ds-bar { position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50%; width: 26px; height: 7px; margin: -3.5px 0 0 -13px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #4a5364, #171c25); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.85); transform-origin: 50% 50%; } .ds-arc-blue .ds-bar-a { transform: rotate(162deg) translateX(107px); } .ds-arc-blue .ds-bar-b { transform: rotate(198deg) translateX(107px); } .ds-arc-white .ds-bar-a { transform: rotate(-18deg) translateX(107px); } .ds-arc-white .ds-bar-b { transform: rotate(18deg) translateX(107px); }

narrative.overview:
The world is a dead fiber-optic tunnel, and light is the only material in it. Nothing here is a painted surface — every visible thing is either emitting, catching a single key light, or falling away into void. This is not a stylistic preference; it is the hard-won result of four rejected attempts at painted surfaces (checkerboard carpets, rungs, painted decals, filled hazard planes). Painted fills read as mud at every value in this palette. Luminous bars over a faint additive haze read as real. Never paint a surface in this world. Draw the light it throws.

The register is cold, luminous, and machined. Chrome is glass and light over dark metal: translucent navy fills, luminous header bands, corner brackets that hold a panel rather than decorate it. Everything is built rather than styled — a hairline speculars-on-machined-edges discipline that came directly from photographic reference (lens barrels, plasma discharge tubes, Marx generators) after two rounds of work were rejected as "too cartoony." What made cartoons: flat fills, colored rim-outline strokes, uniform lighting all the way around a circle, and saturated glow arcs. What fixed it: one world key light everything obeys, matte near-black metal with contrast only at machined edges, and no outlines anywhere.

Density is extreme in the center and empty at the edges. The player's whole field of attention is a bore roughly 88% of the screen's short side, and text, threats, instruments, and story all have to live inside that circle. There is no page, no scroll, no chrome rail — a single canvas, one ring, and the dark beyond it. Everything the system does is in service of a player reading depth, angle, and threat type in under a second.
keyCharacteristics: One key light (LIGHT_A = -TAU * 0.31) that every metal surface in the game obeys
No outlines, ever — form comes from value breaks at machined edges
Color is the rule set, not decoration: hue tells the player which node can kill what
Radial-first geometry; the bore's circle governs layout, type width, and motion
Emitted light over painted fill, in every case, on every surface
Film grain and vignette as the finishing pass, never as a texture layer underneath

rules.name: The Gold Rule
rules.body: Payload Gold appears only where the player gains something: the bonus ribbon, pulse charge, score, the leaderboard, case-file value. Never on a hazard, never as decoration, never as a warm accent for contrast. This rule was paid for — the rim-wall hazard bars shipped in amber, read as inviting and bonus-like, and were recolored to Breach Red the same day. If gold is on screen, the player should be able to move toward it.

rules.name: The Match Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue and Arc White are reserved for the player's two nodes and the enemies keyed to them. No interface element, no marketing surface, and no effect may use a node color on something that is not a node or its matching lock. Ambiguity here is a gameplay bug, not a visual preference.

rules.name: The Calm Bait Rule
rules.body: The most dangerous body in the game is the least saturated one. Threat level is not communicated through visual loudness — it is communicated through learned color meaning. Never brighten Null Graphite to "warn" the player.

rules.name: The Chord Rule
rules.body: All in-bore text is clamped to the ring's clear chord at its own vertical position (ringChord(y)), then shrunk to fit (fitPx). Text never overlaps the ring band, and never wraps to a width the circle can't hold. Copy is authored short so the clamp rarely has to fight it — briefing lines are two lines of roughly forty characters.

rules.name: The Last Pass Rule
rules.body: Overlay text draws as the final pass of the frame. Audiowide is wide and earlier layers used to cover it. Nothing renders on top of copy the player must read.

rules.name: The Never-Animate-Size Rule
rules.body: Text emphasis animates through ctx.scale at steady alpha, never by animating font pixel size. Rounding font px per frame reads as chopping, and combining it with an alpha flicker reads as broken. A breathing hint scales; it does not resize.

rules.name: The Curved Label Rule
rules.body: Text laid on an arc (arcText) stays upright on both halves of the circle, and animated callers lock the flip decision to the element's resting angle so a spin can't toggle orientation mid-flight.

rules.name: The No-HUD Rule
rules.body: Depth and priority never get a HUD element. Range rings, per-enemy countdown tags, flow-line chains, and priority numbers were all built and all reverted as clutter. Urgency lives on the enemy body — an urgency ramp over the final ~1.5 seconds driving LED panic-blink, glow, ripple, and sparks — plus stereo sonar ticks panned to each hostile's angle. If new information needs to reach the player mid-run, it goes on the object or into the sound field, not onto a panel.

rules.name: The Draw-Light Rule
rules.body: Never fill a surface to describe it. Describe it with the light it emits or catches. This is the most expensive lesson in the project: painted hazard carpets were rejected four times before the answer turned out to be a colonnade of luminous bars over an additive haze, with the tunnel still visible through it.

rules.name: The No-Outline Rule
rules.body: No element is ever given a colored rim stroke to define it. Contrast belongs on machined edges — hairline speculars, knurl bands, engraved index ticks.

rules.name: The Glow-Plus-Texture Rule
rules.body: When something must read as energized, add glow and texture, not line-drawn effects. Two styles of drawn electricity (random zigzags, harmonic ribbons) were both rejected; the shipped shield is a full-band glow plus film-grain scintillation composited at two speeds and scales, so the charge appears to boil inside the metal.

rules.name: The Keyed-Corner Rule
rules.body: Every cut-corner panel cuts the same two corners (top-left, bottom-right) in the same direction. A mirrored cut reads as a different manufacturer.

rules.name: The Accumulating Phase Rule
rules.body: Effect phases only ever accumulate (fxPh += dt * rate). Never multiply raw time by an urgency- or state-dependent rate, and never seed an effect from a value that advances. Both mistakes cause visible phase jumps — they shipped once as a strobing "doubled lines" artifact near the ring.

rules.name: The Determinism Rule
rules.body: No visual effect may consume a draw from the campaign's seeded spawn RNG. An extra draw shifts the entire level sequence and breaks replay equality. Derive effect seeds from static properties like spawn angle.

dos: Do obey the single key light (LIGHT_A = -TAU * 0.31) on every metal surface, so far sides fall off and only machined edges catch a speculars.
Do draw light instead of painting fills — luminous bars over additive haze, with the world still visible through them.
Do keep the cut-corner silhouette keyed the same way (top-left, bottom-right) at 8/12/16px.
Do build every instrument from the same track-plus-rails-plus-ticks grammar.
Do clamp in-bore text to the ring chord and shrink it to fit, and draw it as the frame's last pass.
Do reserve Payload Gold for gains only (The Gold Rule).
Do put new mid-run information on the object or in the sound field, never on a HUD panel (The No-HUD Rule).
Do finish with vignette then film grain, both gated behind lowFX.
Do animate emphasis through ctx.scale at steady alpha, never by animating font size.
donts: Don't add a colored rim outline to define a shape. This is the fastest route back to "too cartoony," which has been rejected twice.
Don't light a circular object uniformly all the way around.
Don't use flat fills plus saturated glow arcs as a material.
Don't put gold on a hazard. Amber hazard bars shipped, read as an invitation, and were recolored to Breach Red the same day.
Don't brighten Null Graphite. The node-killer's calm appearance is the trap.
Don't use a node color (Signal Blue, Arc White) on anything that is not a node or its matching lock.
Don't add drawn-line electricity to convey energy — use glow plus texture (both zigzag and harmonic-ribbon filaments were rejected).
Don't add hit-stop or screen shake to routine kills. World flinch reads as bad; kill feedback is burst, rim flash, node recoil, and haptics.
Don't use monospace for anything the player has to read as language.
Don't introduce a melodic riser or pitch slide into the boot sequence — it reads as comical against the tactical register.
Don't re-attempt the kill effect casually. Six iterations have been rejected; prototype options as screenshots or video and let the author pick.
